problem: Prior language-grounded navigation agents map raw observations directly to actions with model-free RL, often in synthetic environments. They ignore environment dynamics, need a lot of data, and generalize poorly to unseen scenes, including in the photo-realistic R2R setting, where Seq2Seq teacher- or student-forcing reaches only about 20% test SR.
motivation: Humans following directions imagine what lies ahead and plan before acting. Model-based RL (Imagination-Augmented Agents, Value Prediction Network) had shown that learned environment models support multi-step lookahead in games, but it had never been applied to real-world vision-and-language navigation. The authors expect that an internal predictive model of future visual states and rewards will help the agent transfer to unseen environments.
key_idea: Add look-ahead modules to a model-free seq2seq VLN policy (Reinforced Planning Ahead, RPA). Each module uses a pretrained environment model that predicts the next ResNet feature state and reward to roll out imagined short trajectories, one per action. These imagined trajectories are encoded and fused with the model-free features to choose the action.
insight: Planning ahead in the abstract feature space mainly helps generalization. Plain model-free RL barely improves over cross-entropy (XE) training on unseen splits (val-unseen SR 21.3→21.5, test 22.1→23.1). Adding the look-ahead path gives a larger jump (val-unseen 24.6, test 25.3), a relative SR gain over XE of 15.5% on val-unseen and 14.5% on test versus only 6.7% on val-seen. The reward ablation (Table 2, model-free RL) shows two things: per-step discounted distance-reduction rewards beat path-level rewards (Global Distance SR 19.0, binary Success 21.3 on val-unseen), and adding the success bonus to the discounted reward gives the best SR (21.5 val-unseen, 41.9 val-seen).
method: Language encoder: word embedding (256) → LSTM (512) → Linear+Tanh, producing word features {w_i}.

Recurrent policy (model-free path): attention LSTM decoder with dot-product attention over words using h_{t-1}. Input is [c_t, s_t (frozen ResNet-152 feature), a_{t-1}], and it outputs [h_t; c_t] as the model-free feature.

Environment model: a linear projection of [s_t, action embedding] feeds a transition MLP with sigmoid output that predicts the 2048-d next ResNet feature s'_{t+1}, and a reward MLP that predicts the scalar reward. It is pretrained with MSE losses (reward loss weight 0.001) on rollouts from a randomized teacher policy (follows the demonstration with p_human=0.95, otherwise acts randomly), then frozen.

Look-ahead modules (model-based path): at every step, run 5 imagined rollouts, one per non-STOP action, as the first action. Subsequent actions come from the shared look-ahead policy (the model-free policy), and the best depth is 2. Each trajectory of predicted states and rewards is encoded by an LSTM (256), and the 5 encodings are concatenated.
Action predictor: an MLP taking [5×256 look-ahead encodings; 1024-d model-free feature] → softmax over 6 low-level actions.

Learning: mixed loss of supervised (teacher-action log-likelihood) and REINFORCE, with the supervised weight decayed from 1.0 to a lower bound of 0.15. The reward is the discounted cumulative per-step reduction in distance to target (γ=0.95) plus a binary success bonus on the final action.

setting.backbone: Frozen ImageNet ResNet-152 features + LSTM attention seq2seq policy, learned environment model and MLP action predictor (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: R2R train split (14,025 instructions). The environment model is pretrained on rollouts in R2R train generated by a randomized teacher policy (p_human=0.95). No extra or augmented data.
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (single forward view, ResNet-152 features); no depth or panorama
setting.action_space: low-level R2R actions on the nav graph: turn left, turn right, camera up, camera down, move forward, stop (max 20 steps)
setting.privileged: none (GT distance-to-target is used only for training rewards; at test time rewards are predicted by the learned environment model)

numbers_note: SPL is not reported (the paper predates its adoption for R2R). Table 2 contains reward-function ablations for the model-free RL agent on val-seen and val-unseen only; they are summarized in insight, not listed as numbers. The look-ahead depth ablation is only stated in text ('best performance is 2'), with no table. Environment-model learning curves appear only in a figure.
results: On R2R, RPA reaches 25.3% SR / 7.53 m NE on test and 24.6% SR / 7.65 m NE on val-unseen. The strongest prior baseline, Seq2Seq student-forcing from Anderson et al., gets 20.4% test and 21.8% val-unseen SR. The authors' own model-free RL agent gets 23.1% test and 21.5% val-unseen SR. Gains from look-ahead are relatively larger on unseen environments than on val-seen (42.9% vs 41.9% SR).
limitations: Absolute gains are small (about 25% test SR) in the low-level single-view action setting. The environment model is pretrained separately and frozen, predicts only ResNet features, and its reward prediction is noisy because rewards are sparse.
There is no quantitative ablation of look-ahead depth or number of rollouts, no SPL or efficiency metric, and no variance across runs.

The stated failure modes remain unsolved: out-of-vocabulary words, ambiguous instructions in complex unseen scenes, and error accumulation after a wrong action. The authors also note that camera up/down actions are rarely used, reflecting a limitation of R2R's action distribution.
builds_on: REINFORCE with mixed loss (MIXER, Ranzato et al.)
